summary: MF-016: mutation kill test (oracle 4). Coverage derived from port/invariant declarations every run; control run refuses a red corpus; kill_rate_floor gate fails below floor with no waiver; survivors point at the variable and action to refine; abstraction validator via --baseline/--compare. Mechanism built and unit/adapter/example-validated; empirical proof over this repository's corpus deferred to MF-023 per epic policy.

assertions: kill rate is computed against kill_rate_floor from budgets and gates nonzero below it.
mutants, kill matrix, and surviving-mutant analysis land under ticket evidence.
distributed_history carries a worked kill test in local mode.
commands: python3 scripts/tla_spec_dev.py --spec-root specs run spec-unit-tests --ticket MF-016

adapters: spec-unit adapter proving a seeded fault is killed and reported

implementation_scope: scripts/run_kill_test.py (new) or documented procedure with runner support
ticket.objective: Kill-test support: documented and CLI-assisted seeding of at least one fault per port and one per invariant, distilled-corpus run, kill_rate_floor gate from manifest budgets, evidence storage (mutants, kill matrix, surviving-mutant analysis), onboarding/promotion as required kill-test moments, kill-rate before/after comparison across model revisions so the kill test doubles as the abstraction validator (references/architecture_tractability.md), and a worked kill test in distributed_history. See tickets/016-mutation-kill-test.md.
outcome: DEVIATION 1 (plan entry not binding, known-stale #33): desired_actions/model_state prescribed the kill_test fact and RunKillTest action, both landed. Added beyond the entry: invariant KillTestVerdictRequiresBudgets, because RunKillTest guards on setup_phase >= 4 - the floor it gates against IS a budget, and reading kill_rate_floor before budgets are recorded would measure against a default nobody negotiated. That addition immediately grew the required-boundary set 18 -> 19 and made the kill test refuse until a mutant covered it: the coverage mechanism applying to its own oracle.

DEVIATION 1b: the verdict domain is 4-valued (unknown/pass/below_floor/incomplete_catalog) rather than the entry's not-run/pass/fail, on the MF-027 criterion - below_floor and incomplete_catalog have different remedies (refine the model at the survivor's named variable vs. seed a fault for an uncovered boundary) and select different result.next strings. All three non-unknown values were confirmed individually reachable by TLC before the domain was fixed at four.

DEVIATION 2: the promotion INTERLOCK is deliberately NOT modelled. CloseTicket does not require kill_test = pass, because the shipped close ticket does not enforce it and kill-test RUNS are deferred to MF-023. Gating close on a run that cannot happen would block every ticket close including this one, and writing the guard in anyway would make the model assert a behaviour the program lacks - precisely the defect oracle 4 exists to detect. The interlock lands with the runs.

DEVIATION 3: examples/run_distributed_history_validation.py --mode local is NOT green and could not have been. Case generation for the example's External model is refused by a PRE-EXISTING complexity-gate finding (C2 touched by 9 actions, exceeding max_component_actions 8), verified by re-running with this ticket's files removed. Not worked around; no --allow-over-budget. The worked kill test was validated directly end-to-end against the real internal corpus instead.

MOST IMPORTANT FINDING: the first end-to-end run of the worked example scored a perfect 7/7 kill rate that was entirely SPURIOUS. The corpus was already failing an unrelated effect-oracle dead_surface finding before any mutant was seeded, and since killed means the corpus run failed, every mutant was recorded as killed by that one pre-existing failure. A kill test without a control run reports its most flattering number exactly when the corpus is most broken. control_run() and the control_failed verdict were added because of this; it dominates every other verdict, computes no rate, seeds nothing, and has no skip flag.

The dead_surface finding was itself real: the example manifest first declared five filesystem.write ports that EcommerceStore never crosses (in-memory sqlite). Per governing rule 4 the false declarations were REMOVED rather than the finding suppressed - a port the program never crosses is not a richer model, it is a wrong one.

The corrected worked example then measured 0.571 (4/7) against the 0.8 floor with a GREEN control - BELOW FLOOR, three genuine survivors, each with an actionable pointer (projections/ProjectOrder, orders/Checkout, responses/SubmitCreateAccount). The floor was NOT lowered and the survivors were NOT waived; validate_kill_test() asserts the strict outcome and keeps failing until the example's representation is actually refined. That refinement is MF-023's work.

COMPLEXITY DELTA recorded jointly with retention evidence: 8 -> 9 variables, bound 174,960 -> 699,840 (x4), TLC 1,067,828 -> 5,619,356 generated / 49,875 -> 231,621 distinct / depth 24 -> 25. That is 46.3% of the negotiated max_distinct_states 500,000, up from 10.0% - a much larger consumption than 'a gate variable is affordable' suggested, reported as measured rather than estimated. Both caps still pass. Repository unit tests 315 -> 373.

STANDING OBJECTIVE - searched, found a measured 26.2% reduction, REFUSED it. Collapsing kill_test to 3 values gives 171,039 distinct (from 231,621) at unchanged depth 25. Refused on MF-027's own standard: it deletes an externally-visible distinction with a distinct remedy and a distinct result.next. RETENTION EVIDENCE: each of pass / below_floor / incomplete_catalog was confirmed individually reachable by TLC (invariant-violation probe), so the 4-value domain represents the reachable set exactly - a cheaper representation exists but it is not a re-representation.

ADVISORY, owner approval required, NOT applied: analyze complexity now recommends projecting [lastCommand, result] (no invariant reads them) and notes the move is legitimate iff the kill rate holds - which is the check this ticket built (--compare). lastCommand is the only model variable with no seeded mutant and no invariant, justified solely by an effect; it is the weakest-justified element and the natural first candidate if the owner wants the bound reduced.

LIVE FINDING, not worked around: C1 is now touched by 14 actions (was 13); RunKillTest is the 14th. Same TRUE finding about the undecomposed single-module baseline, resolved at the root by MF-023. No budget renegotiated, no override used.

MF-027 CONSTRAINT CONFIRMED: the runner spawns a child process per mutant, so under the effect oracle a kill-test run is unobservable, not clean. Neither oracle was relaxed; three resolution options are written up for MF-023 in results/DEFERRED-TO-MF-023.md.

DEFERRAL STATED PLAINLY: no mutant in specs/current/kill_mutants.toml has ever been run against this repository's own corpus, because case generation is deferred. The 19 mutants are verified to apply uniquely, to be behavioural rather than syntactic, and to restore byte-identically - but whether the corpus KILLS them is the open empirical question. results/DEFERRED-TO-MF-023.md states exactly what MF-023 must run.
Negotiated max_distinct_states 500000 and all 13 rationale comment lines verified present in specs/current, ticket desired/ and ticket current/ both before and after promotion.
